key_insight: The paper separates exploration from optimization in RLVR by using novelty only for generating candidate solutions, then distilling filtered correct trajectories into a student trained without novelty pressure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a safer way to boost reasoning diversity in language models without letting novelty incentives destabilize the main policy during reinforcement learning.
method: Train one or more explorer policies with a novelty bonus in the reward.
Filter explorer trajectories for correctness and quality.
Distill the filtered trajectories into a separate student policy and repeat in alternating rounds.
evidence_signal: Across seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model families, ExpDis outperforms DAPO at the same wall-clock budget and improves pass@$k$ scaling.
watch_item: Filtering and distillation add pipeline complexity, and the approach still depends on reliable verifiers to identify correct, high-quality exploratory trajectories.
paper_title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
